title: Microstructural evolutions and mechanical properties of multilayered 1060Al/Al-Al2O3 composites fabricated by cold spraying and accumulative roll bonding
InformationInFigures: Yes. Particle size distribution (Fig. 2), stress-strain curve (Fig. 8). deposition info (Fig. 1)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Al powder had a mostly spherical morphology, with some irregularities and/or satellite particles. Al2O3 particles have an angular morphology. low in impurities. mixture is evenly dispersed.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: Powder sizes were reported seperately. Average Al2O3 particle size was 27.64 μm, the size range was 11-60 μm, and the D10, D50, and D90 values were 16 μm, 26 μm, and 41 μm resp.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Material_Composition: 0.26 wt% Fe, 0.13 wt% Si, 0.013 wt% Ti, Bal. Al
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: wire-brushed to remove the impurities and increase the surface roughness

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Annealed at 450°C for 50 minutes in a muffle furnace
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The powder was uniformly mixed in a mechanically rotating cylinder with 80 mm diameter for 2 h. For microstructural characterization, samples were prepared by mechanical grinding and polishing on the rolling direction-normal direction (RD-ND) planes.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: well-bonded interface between the 1060Al plate and the deposited layer, without conspicuous voids or cracks. but, voids can be clearly observed at the granular boundary in the deposited layer, and visible cracks on the Al2O3 particles caused by severe plastic deformation. high percentage of LAGBs remain, indicating that there is large strain energy stored.

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Deposit as annealed at 450°C for 50 minutes in a muffle furnace. An 1060 Al substrate plate with no deposits was also annealed at 450°C for 50 minutes in a muffle furnace before being used for the rolling process. The annealed deposit was stacked under the annealed substrate plate. Both layers underwent wire brushing surface treatment before. The layers were riveted together and pre-heated in a muffle furnace at 380°C for 8 minutes. Accumulative roll bonding (ARB) was performed using a two-high rolling mill with a 170 mm diameter roller, where the sample was rolled with 50% reduction in one-pass without lubricant. Cooled to room temperature.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The powder was uniformly mixed in a mechanically rotating cylinder with 80 mm diameter for 2 h. For microstructural characterization, samples were prepared by mechanical grinding and polishing on the rolling direction-normal direction (RD-ND) planes.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: internal defects of the composites are somewhat compensated, with fewer voids observed in the matrix. 45% HAGBs. there are several boundaries consisting of incomplete HAGBs and fine grains. This illustrates the incomplete process of the transformation from LAGBs to HAGBs, which is usually associated with continuous dynamic recrystallization. Additionally, a typical grain-bulging feature associated with discontinuous dynamic recrystallization was observed.
